item.title: Plug Power Plans Hydrogen Offering in Top US Power-Grid Auction
item.description: Plug Power Inc. is planning to offer hydrogen electricity in a potential special auction by the biggest US power grid in the scramble to feed the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Trump Urges Latin America to Use Military Against Cartels
item.description: President Donald Trump told a group of Latin American leaders that they need to work with the US to target drug trafficking cartels as he sought to bolster US leadership in the region.

item.title: Queues, Price Hikes and Shortages as Asia Battles Fuel Crunch
item.description: From Thai farmers racing for diesel to Indian refinery executives monitoring the Persian Gulf through the night, energy buyers across import-dependent Asia are feeling the impact of a dramatic crunch.

item.title: US Offers $20 Billion Reinsurance Plan to Spur Gulf Oil Flow
item.description: The Trump administration announced a $20 billion reinsurance program aimed at reviving shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic has all but stopped amid the US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

item.title: US Inflation Gauges Likely Diverged Before War in Iran
item.description: A pair of inflation reports, including the Federal Reserve’s preferred price gauge, surface in the coming week after a dismal February jobs report that challenged perceptions the labor market is stabilizing.

item.title: Australia Weighs Request From Gulf Nations for Military Support
item.description: Australia said it is assessing a request from Gulf nations for defensive military support to protect them against Iranian drone and missile attacks.

item.title: China Eyes ‘Landmark’ Year for US Ties, Urges End to Iran War
item.description: China’s top diplomat signaled that Beijing is prioritizing a stabilization of ties with Washington, even as he issued a pointed critique of US military actions in the Middle East.

item.title: Bank of England May Be Wary of Looking Past Another Energy Shock
item.description: Later this week, Bank of England policymakers will receive their first briefings as preparations for the March 19 interest-rate decision get under way. The question is how far they are willing to tolerate an energy-price shock that is threatening to blow inflation off course.
